plain: If you see a bear, don't run, since sudden movement can trigger a chase response and you cannot outrun a bear, which can reach speeds of 30 mph. Don't climb a tree either, as both black bears and grizzlies can climb well, or in the grizzly's case, still reach you at the base. Avoid direct sustained eye contact, since bears can perceive it as a threat or challenge, and don't approach the bear for a photo or to get closer, no matter how calm it seems. Don't scream or make sudden loud noises that could startle it into a defensive reaction, and never get between a mother bear and her cubs. Lastly, don't leave food or trash behind that could reinforce the bear's association between humans and easy meals.

Calf raises, done on a step for a fuller range of motion, build the calves with no equipment needed. Step-ups onto a sturdy chair or bench also build strength and endurance simultaneously.

When you include marine protected areas along its coasts, Costa Rica has also significantly expanded ocean protection in recent years, part of a broader national commitment to conservation dating back to the 1970s. plain: The four suits on a standard deck of cards, hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades, are widely believed to represent the four classes of medieval society in the French card tradition that became the modern standard. Hearts symbolized the clergy, representing the church. Diamonds, shaped like tiles or paving stones, represented the merchant or wealthy trading class. Clubs, taking their name and shape from a stylized clover, stood for the peasantry or agricultural workers. Spades, resembling the tip of a spear or sword, represented the nobility and military class. This French design, developed in the 15th century, replaced earlier suit systems used in Italian, Spanish, and German playing cards, and eventually became the international standard through trade and colonial influence.

plain: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, covering approximately 17.1 million square kilometers, which is nearly twice the size of Canada, the second-largest country. Russia spans eleven time zones and stretches across both Eastern Europe and northern Asia, bordering fourteen countries and touching both the Arctic and Pacific Oceans. Despite its enormous size, much of Russia's territory, particularly Siberia, is sparsely populated due to its harsh, cold climate, and most of the country's roughly 144 million people live in the western, European part of the country. If ranked by population instead of area, Russia would fall far down the list, well behind countries like India, China, and the United States.

plain: A Haft-sin is a traditional table setting for Nowruz, the Persian New Year, and it traditionally includes seven items that begin with the Persian letter sin (S), each symbolizing something meaningful for the year ahead. Sabzeh, sprouted wheat or lentil grass, represents rebirth and growth. Samanu, a sweet wheat pudding, symbolizes affluence and fertility. Senjed, dried oleaster fruit, represents love. Seer, garlic, symbolizes health and medicine. Seeb, apples, represent beauty and health. Somaq, sumac berries, represent the sunrise and the victory of good over evil. Serkeh, vinegar, represents patience and the wisdom that comes with age. Many families also include a mirror, candles, painted eggs, a bowl of water with goldfish, and coins to enrich the table further.

plain: Mozzarella and cheddar differ significantly in texture, flavor, and how they're made. Mozzarella is a fresh, soft cheese traditionally made from buffalo or cow's milk using a stretching technique called pasta filata, giving it a stringy, elastic texture and a mild, milky flavor; it's typically eaten fresh or melted, especially on pizza, where it becomes gooey and stretchy. Cheddar, by contrast, is an aged, firm cheese with a much sharper, more complex flavor that intensifies the longer it's aged, ranging from mild, a few months, to extra sharp, a year or more. plain: Andy Warhol's Oxidation Paintings, often nicknamed the piss paintings, were created in the late 1970s by having friends, assistants, and visitors to his studio urinate onto canvases that had been pre-coated with metallic copper paint. The uric acid in the urine chemically reacted with the copper pigment, oxidizing it and creating unpredictable green, blue, and rust-colored patterns and textures across the canvas as it dried. Warhol reportedly sometimes added vitamins or specific foods to the diets of his collaborators beforehand to influence the color of the resulting reactions, treating the whole process almost like a controlled chemistry experiment. The series was part of Warhol's broader interest in chance and removing the artist's own hand from the creative process.

It can also happen if you're not flexing your ankles and knees forward enough, causing your center of mass to fall behind your base of support. To fix it, focus on staying centered or slightly forward throughout the whole turn and actively extending your ankles as you finish.
